_note: Draft English of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Bereshit 28 (Jacob's ladder dream). Saadia-specific moves: v.3 'אלטאיק אלכאפי' = 'the Sufficient Power' (= B17:1 — for El Shaddai); v.11 'אלמוצ'ע אלכ'אץ' = 'the special/specific place' (Saadia gives 'the place' a definite-article reading); v.13 'נור אללה ואקף אמאמה' = 'the light of God standing before him' (anti-anthropomorphic — not God Himself, but His light/glory; cf. B17:22, B18:33); v.16 'נור אללה' similarly; v.17 'מא הד'א אלא בית אללה' = 'this is none but God's house'; v.21 'ולייא' = 'my patron/guardian' (substitutes for אלהים).

translations.1: And Isaac called Jacob, and blessed him, and commanded him, and said to him: 'You shall not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan.
translations.2: Arise, go to Paddan-Aram, to the house of Bethuel your grandfather, and take for yourself from there a wife from the daughters of Laban, your mother's brother.
translations.3: And the Sufficient Power shall bless you, and make you grow, and multiply you; and there shall be from you a host of nations.
translations.4: And He shall give you the blessing of Abraham — to you and to your offspring with you — to possess the land of your dwelling, which God gave to Abraham.'
translations.5: And Isaac sent Jacob; and he went to Paddan-Aram, to Laban the son of Bethuel the Aramean, the brother of Rebekah, the mother of Jacob and Esau.
translations.6: And Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob, and had sent him to Paddan-Aram to take a wife for him from there — when he blessed him, and commanded him, saying: 'You shall not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan';
translations.7: and that Jacob had accepted from his father and his mother, and had gone to Paddan-Aram.
translations.8: And when Esau saw that the daughters of Canaan were evil in the sight of Isaac his father,
translations.9: Esau went to Ishmael, and took Mahalath, the daughter of Ishmael the son of Abraham, the sister of Nebayot, in addition to his wives — and she became his wife.
translations.10: Then Jacob went out from Beer-Sheba, to go to Haran.
translations.11: And he came to the special place, and lodged there — for the sun had set. And he took of the stones of the place, and made it a pillow, and slept there.
translations.12: And he saw a dream — and behold, a ladder set upon the earth, and its top approaching the sky; and behold, the angels of God ascending and descending upon it.
translations.13: And behold, the light of God was standing before him, and He said: 'I am God, the God of Abraham your father, and the God of Isaac. The land upon which you are sleeping — to you I shall give it, and to your offspring.
translations.14: And your offspring shall be like the dust of the earth; and you shall spread westward and eastward and northward and southward; and in you shall be blessed all the clans of the earth — and in your offspring.
translations.15: And behold, I am with you, and I shall keep you wherever you walk; and I shall bring you back to this land — I shall not leave you until I have done for you what I have spoken to you.'
translations.16: And Jacob awoke from his sleep, and said: 'Behold — the light of God is in this place, and I did not know.'
translations.17: And he was afraid, and said: 'How awesome is this place! And this is none but the house of God, and this is the gate of the sky.'
translations.18: And Jacob rose early in the morning, and took the stone which he had made a pillow, and set it up as a pillar; and he poured oil upon its top.
translations.19: And he named that place Beth-El; and the name of the town had been Luz at first.
translations.20: And Jacob vowed a vow, and said: 'If God shall be with me, and keep me in this way which I am going, and grant me bread to eat and a garment to wear,
translations.21: and I return in peace to my father's house — then God shall be my Patron;
translations.22: and this stone, which I have set up as a pillar, shall be for me the house of God; and of all that You grant me, I shall tithe to You.'
